descriptionChirho: The nape or back of the neck as shown when turning away, used in contexts of fleeing from enemies or turning one's back on God in rejection.
The neck as the seat of stubbornness in the idiom qesheh-orep (stiff-necked), describing obstinate refusal to submit to God's will or correction.
The literal back of the neck as an anatomical body part in non-idiomatic contexts such as striking, grasping, or physical description and comparison.
